about: What this member said on the floor, from the Congressional Record: their own words only, and of those the sentences that name an alignment question's phrases or make a commitment. Written by npm run record:collect (scripts/collect-record.mjs).
name: Gabe Vasquez

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: WAR IN IRAN IS IMPACTING NEW MEXICANS
statements.title: WAR IN IRAN IS IMPACTING NEW MEXICANS
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today to put in the simplest of terms how the President's war in Iran is impacting New Mexicans.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: WATER IS LIFE
statements.title: WATER IS LIFE
sentences: For generations, ranching families in this border community have relied on water from the Mimbres and Hachita Basin to sustain their herds and their way of life.

DHS contractors today are drilling deep new wells in Luna County for border wall construction, depleting this vital water source with no regard for permitting, State law, or the impact to border ranchers.
Mr. Speaker, we all support border security, but we don't support unauthorized well drilling that's draining precious resources.
I stand with our ranchers. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: AN ICE OFFICER SHOT HIM
statements.title: AN ICE OFFICER SHOT HIM
sentences: He should have sat in his backyard, as he did every afternoon, listening to his music and playing with his dog.
And 7 days later we have no body camera footage, no dash camera footage, and zero accountability.
Well, in America, there is no death penalty for looking like someone else and driving to work, and yet here we are.
I come from the border and from a family of immigrants, and I know the Lorenzos of this country--in Texas, in New Mexico, here in Washington, and across the nation.
In his honor--and in honor of Renee, Alex, and the young man we lost yesterday in Maine--we will not rest until every family in this country can wait for their loved ones at the table, without fear.
And today I give this speech in Spanish and English, without fear, to reinforce that we are a nation of immigrants, and we will continue to be a nation of immigrants.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: GUTTING U.S. FOREST SERVICE RESOURCES
statements.title: GUTTING U.S. FOREST SERVICE RESOURCES
sentences: What I do see is another backdoor move by this administration to push forward an anti-public lands agenda that discards career staff, under- resources our land agencies, and prioritizes corporations rather than focusing on combating wildfires, wildlife habitat, rural communities, and the growing outdoor recreation economy.
Madam Speaker, today, I rise in opposition to this administration's plan to completely gut the U.S. Forest Service, move its headquarters to Utah, and shutter 57 research stations.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TAKEOVER OF GREENLAND
statements.title: TAKEOVER OF GREENLAND
sentences: The time is now in which our true character is being tested, and my Republican colleagues must decide if we will honor those who have gone before us or betray their legacy and our deepest values.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FOCUSING ON REAL RESULTS
statements.title: FOCUSING ON REAL RESULTS
sentences: My district is one of the largest districts in the country, larger than the State of Pennsylvania, and includes major cities, border towns, Tribal communities, and rural counties that often feel forgotten by Washington.
For families waiting on Social Security, veterans navigating the VA, or seniors dealing with the IRS, that help was immediate and personal.

From talking to students in Deming, meeting with Tribal leaders in Zuni Pueblo, hosting a carne asada with oil workers in Carlsbad, and convening roundtables with police departments in Albuquerque, this is a big district with many needs, and advocacy doesn't just start at the Capitol steps.

I have also worked hard to secure Federal investments across New Mexico, from addressing homelessness to investing in workplace training, to launching a new express bus service connecting Las Cruces to El Paso.
The good people of New Mexico elected me to do a job, and I intend to do it; not with red or blue solutions, but practical solutions that are rooted in the real lives of the people who I represent.
Public lands are one of our Nation's best ideas, and I intend to keep it that way.
I will continue showing up, fighting for them, and doing the work they sent me here to do. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SECURE RURAL SCHOOLS REAUTHORIZATION ACT OF 2025
statements.title: SECURE RURAL SCHOOLS REAUTHORIZATION ACT OF 2025
sentences: It ensured that public schools could keep teachers in the classroom, that buses could run safe routes on rural roads, and that county governments could plan long-term budgets with certainty.

They have brought in tours from all across the country to see the darkest skies in the country in what is an International Dark Skies Sanctuary and one of the most breathtaking trails that one can experience in our Nation's first wilderness.
The Senate has already passed this reauthorization, and I urge my colleagues to help us finish the job and send the bill to the President's desk for his signature.
Mr. Speaker, I am proud to vote in favor of the SRS Reauthorization Act, and I urge my colleagues to join me in its passage.
The fact that we will today shows just how important we all know it is to stand up for our rural communities.
I urge my colleagues to support this bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DEFENDING THE ARCTIC REFUGE
statements.title: DEFENDING THE ARCTIC REFUGE
sentences: I rise today to urge my colleagues to vote ``no'' on S.J. Res. 80 and H.J. Res. 131, two proposals that would forever alter the Coastal Plain of the Arctic refuge and the special areas of the western Arctic in the great State of Alaska.
The Arctic refuge, the homeland of Gwich'in and the Inupiat people, offers unmatched, truly wild fishing and hunting opportunities for all Americans.

These lands, the birthing and calving grounds of the Porcupine caribou herd, have been at the center of national debate for more than a century, ever since Republican President Theodore Roosevelt established the National Wildlife Refuge System and dedicated himself to protecting wild places and the wildlife that depend on them.
Most importantly, these lands have provided sustenance to the Gwich'in and Inupiat peoples since time immemorial.

That is why, as a hunter, an angler, and someone who cares deeply about our Nation's incomparable system of public lands and wildlife habitat, I can't support the reckless destruction of the Arctic tundra and the Coastal Plain.

It would be much easier for them if the last remaining musk ox hadn't survived the Ice Age or if the Porcupine caribou herd simply went extinct, just to add a few dollars to their pockets today without giving a damn about tomorrow.
Now, much to my dismay, this administration has already issued an executive order to rescind the Coastal Plain leasing program, and the Department of the Interior has already done just that.

If, like me, you still believe in bipartisanship and revere the greats like Teddy Roosevelt, who fought to protect special places like America's Arctic, and you dream that someday you or one of your children can hunt wild ptarmigan on the Coastal Plain, catch an Arctic char on the Canning River, or harvest caribou in the Brooks Range, you should vote against these bills and honor the voices of the indigenous communities and American citizens who depend on this land for survival.
I urge my colleagues to vote ``no'' on H.J. Res. 131. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE BUREAU OF LAND MANAGEMENT RELATING TO "BUFFALO FIELD OFFICE RECORD OF DECISION AND APPROVED RES
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE BUREAU OF LAND MANAGEMENT RELATING TO "BUFFALO FIELD OFFICE RECORD OF DECISION AND APPROVED RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PLAN AMENDMENT"
sentences: In 2017, when the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge's Coastal Plain was first officially opened to drilling, supporters promised that the sale would raise significant revenue.
The first mandated lease sale brought in less than 1 percent of the $2.2 billion that Congress was told to expect, less than 1 percent.
That burdened taxpayers with an additional $2 billion in national debt.

The Coastal Plain is too remote, too costly, and too risky to make drilling financially feasible, especially when we already produce record oil and gas volumes elsewhere at a far lower cost to taxpayers, including in my district, the Permian Basin.
The Arctic refuge is the only national wildlife refuge that protects a complete Arctic ecosystem.
When you catch your first Arctic char in the Canning River on the Coastal Plain, it is a moment you will never forget as an American.
These lands have provided sustenance to the Gwich'in and the Inupiat peoples for millennia.

By treating every resource management plan as a rule that is subject to the CRA, Congress is throwing the legal status of every oil and gas lease, every grazing permit, and recreational activity across the West into question.
They have already opened up the Coastal Plain, so why do this?
Today, I rise in opposition to all the CRAs, but in particular, I want to talk about one very special place.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HIGHLIGHTING THE LAPSE IN SECURE RURAL SCHOOLS FUNDING
statements.title: HIGHLIGHTING THE LAPSE IN SECURE RURAL SCHOOLS FUNDING
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to support the Secure Rural Schools Reauthorization Act so that rural communities in New Mexico and across the country are not forgotten and left behind without access to basic needs. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NATIONAL POLICE WEEK
statements.title: NATIONAL POLICE WEEK
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today during National Police Week to honor the courageous law enforcement officers from New Mexico who have made the ultimate sacrifice in service to our communities.
Every day across our country and in my home State, law enforcement officers wake up, put on the badge, and commit themselves to protecting our neighbors.

This year, three officers from New Mexico are being added to the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial wall here in Washington: Corrections Officer Roberto Rodriguez of Dona Ana County, Patrol Officer Jonah Hernandez of the Las Cruces Police Department, and Patrolman Justin C. Hare of the New Mexico State Police.

I also want to honor those who recently did not have the opportunity to come home: Las Cruces Police Officer J.R. Stewart, Albuquerque Police Officer Bianca Quintana, Alamogordo Police Officer Anthony ``Tony'' Ferguson, Alamogordo Patrolman James M. Sides, New Mexico State Police Officer Darian Jarrott, and Curry County Sheriff Michael Reeves.
That means investing in officer safety, mental health, and wellness.
Choosing a life of service and law enforcement is not easy.
Chief Story is from the Las Cruces Police Department, my hometown, and he is someone I was proud to serve with in local government.
Chief Story has spent over 18 years in service to Las Cruces, rising through the ranks from cadet to chief of police.
He brought together law enforcement, emergency responders, and community leaders, not just to respond, but to begin the healing of our community.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ENSURING VETERANS RECEIVE CARE THEY EARNED
statements.title: ENSURING VETERANS RECEIVE CARE THEY EARNED
sentences: These cuts include doctors, mental health professionals, and benefits processors.
That is why I am introducing a package of bills focused on real solutions: expanding healthcare access, improving transportation, and easing financial burdens for veterans pursuing an education.
That is why I am proud to introduce these crucial bills and to host Roland ``Coopdawg'' Cooper today.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to support these bills.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DIRE CONSEQUENCES OF FUNDING FREEZE AND MASS FIRINGS
statements.title: DIRE CONSEQUENCES OF FUNDING FREEZE AND MASS FIRINGS
sentences: How does firing somebody making less than $40,000 a year solve the debt crisis?

As Elon Musk is busy firing thousands of New Mexicans, the Republican majority is preparing today a budget that offers American taxpayer dollars to give massive tax breaks for millionaires and billionaires.
I hope that my colleagues can justify eliminating a $40,000 Federal job at a national park for wildfire prevention so that a millionaire can take another summer vacation to Aruba.
I urge my colleagues to recognize the human cost of these reckless firings and funding freezes.
